chunks: Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:
The blood money for a Jew and a Christian is four thousand, four thousand, and the blood money for a Magian is eight hundred dirhams.
And he said: Indeed, the Magians have a book called Jamasf.

key_terms.جَامَاسْفُ: The name of the book mentioned for the Magians
key_terms.دِرْهَمٍ: A silver coin used here as the unit of legal compensation
key_terms.دِيَةُ النَّصْرَانِيِّ: The prescribed blood money for a Christian person
key_terms.دِيَةُ الْمَجُوسِيِّ: The prescribed blood money for a Magian (Zoroastrian)
key_terms.دِيَةُ الْيَهُودِيِّ: The prescribed blood money for a Jewish person

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the diyyah of Jews, Christians, and Magians?
ai.summary: This hadith states the legal amounts of diyyah for a Jew, a Christian, and a Magian within the discussed fiqh context. It also notes that the Magians possess a scripture known as Jamasf, indicating their recognition as a community with a book.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5252 - Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Abu Baṣir, who reported from Abu Abdullah (as) that he said:
"The blood money (diyyah) for a Jew and a Christian is four thousand (dirhams), four thousand (dirhams), and the blood money for a Magian (Zoroastrian) is eight hundred dirhams."
Imam (as) also said: "Indeed, the Magians have a book called Jamaspf."
